GO:0005085.name: guanyl-nucleotide exchange factor activity
GO:0005085.definition: Stimulates the exchange of GDP to GTP on a signaling GTPase, changing its conformation to its active form. Guanine nucleotide exchange factors (GEFs) act by stimulating the release of guanosine diphosphate (GDP) to allow binding of guanosine triphosphate (GTP), which is more abundant in the cell under normal cellular physiological conditions.

GO:0005086.name: guanyl-nucleotide exchange factor activity
GO:0005086.definition: Stimulates the exchange of GDP to GTP on a signaling GTPase, changing its conformation to its active form. Guanine nucleotide exchange factors (GEFs) act by stimulating the release of guanosine diphosphate (GDP) to allow binding of guanosine triphosphate (GTP), which is more abundant in the cell under normal cellular physiological conditions.

GO:0005096.name: GTPase activator activity
GO:0005096.definition: Binds to and increases the activity of a GTPase, an enzyme that catalyzes the hydrolysis of GTP.
GO:0005096.comment: Note that the name Sar derives from 'secretion-associated, Ras-related'.

GO:0034260.name: negative regulation of GTPase activity
GO:0034260.definition: Any process that stops or reduces the rate of GTP hydrolysis by a GTPase.
GO:0034260.comment: An example of this is P2xA in Dictyostelium (UniProt symbol Q86JM7) in PMID:24335649.

GO:0043547.name: positive regulation of GTPase activity
GO:0043547.definition: Any process that activates or increases the activity of a GTPase.

GO:0030532.name: small nuclear ribonucleoprotein complex
GO:0030532.definition: A ribonucleoprotein complex that contains at least one RNA of the small nuclear RNA (snRNA) class and as well as its associated proteins. These are typically named after the snRNA(s) they contain, e.g. U1 snRNP, U4/U6 snRNP, or 7SK snRNP. Many, of these complexes become part of the spliceosome involved in splicing of nuclear mRNAs. Others are involved in regulation of transcription elongation or 3'-end processing of replication-dependent histone pre-mRNAs.

GO:0005732.name: sno(s)RNA-containing ribonucleoprotein complex
GO:0005732.definition: A ribonucleoprotein complex that contains an RNA molecule of the snoRNA family and associated proteins. Many are involved in a step of processing of rRNA molecules: cleavage, 2'-O-methylation, or pseudouridylation, but other RNA types can be targets as well. The majority fall into one of two classes, box C/D type or box H/ACA type, which are conserved across eukaryotes and archaea. Other members include the telomerase RNA and the ribonuclease MRP RNA.
GO:0005732.comment: Note that 'nucleolar' in the name acronym 'snoRNA' is part of the RNA family designation 'small nucleolar', and does not reflect the location of the complex. Both box C/D type and box H/ACA RNAs are found in Archaea (where they are referred to as sRNAs) as well as in Eukaryota. In eukaryotes, box H/ACA RNAs are found in both nucleolar-localized snoRNP complexes and in Cajal body-localized scaRNP complexes.

GO:0031428.name: box C/D methylation guide snoRNP complex
GO:0031428.definition: A ribonucleoprotein complex containing a box C/D type RNA that is capable of ribose-2'-O-methylation of target RNAs. Box C/D type RNAs are widespread in eukaryotes and in Archaea, suggesting that an RNA-based guide mechanism for directing specific RNA 2'-O-ribose methylations was present in the common ancestor of Archaea and Eukarya.

GO:0032012.name: regulation of ARF protein signal transduction
GO:0032012.definition: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of ARF protein signal transduction.

GO:0016192.name: vesicle-mediated transport
GO:0016192.definition: A cellular transport process in which transported substances are moved in membrane-bounded vesicles; transported substances are enclosed in the vesicle lumen or located in the vesicle membrane. The process begins with a step that directs a substance to the forming vesicle, and includes vesicle budding and coating. Vesicles are then targeted to, and fuse with, an acceptor membrane.

GO:0042147.name: retrograde transport, endosome to Golgi
GO:0042147.definition: The directed movement of membrane-bounded vesicles from endosomes back to the trans-Golgi network where they are recycled for further rounds of transport.

GO:0034237.name: protein kinase A regulatory subunit binding
GO:0034237.definition: Binding to one or both of the regulatory subunits of protein kinase A.

GO:0017022.name: myosin binding
GO:0017022.definition: Binding to a myosin; myosins are any of a superfamily of molecular motor proteins that bind to actin and use the energy of ATP hydrolysis to generate force and movement along actin filaments.

GO:0090303.name: positive regulation of wound healing
GO:0090303.definition: Any process that increases the rate, frequency, or extent of the series of events that restore integrity to a damaged tissue, following an injury.

GO:0030837.name: negative regulation of actin filament polymerization
GO:0030837.definition: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of actin polymerization.
GO:0030837.comment: Note that this term was split from 'negative regulation of actin polymerization and/or depolymerization ; GO:0045757' (sibling term 'negative regulation of actin depolymerization ; GO:0030835').

GO:0009101.name: glycoprotein biosynthetic process
GO:0009101.definition: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of glycoproteins, a protein that contains covalently bound glycose (i.e. monosaccharide) residues; the glycose occurs most commonly as oligosaccharide or fairly small polysaccharide but occasionally as monosaccharide.

GO:0007030.name: Golgi organization
GO:0007030.definition: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of the Golgi apparatus.

GO:0010256.name: endomembrane system organization
GO:0010256.definition: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of the endomembrane system.

GO:0006887.name: exocytosis
GO:0006887.definition: A process of secretion by a cell that results in the release of intracellular molecules (e.g. hormones, matrix proteins) contained within a membrane-bounded vesicle. Exocytosis can occur either by full fusion, when the vesicle collapses into the plasma membrane, or by a kiss-and-run mechanism that involves the formation of a transient contact, a pore, between a granule (for example of chromaffin cells) and the plasma membrane. The latter process most of the time leads to only partial secretion of the granule content. Exocytosis begins with steps that prepare vesicles for fusion with the membrane (tethering and docking) and ends when molecules are secreted from the cell.

GO:2000114.name: regulation of establishment of cell polarity
GO:2000114.definition: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of establishment of cell polarity.

GO:0031175.name: neuron projection development
GO:0031175.definition: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a neuron projection over time, from its formation to the mature structure. A neuron projection is any process extending from a neural cell, such as axons or dendrites (collectively called neurites).

GO:0051897.name: positive regulation of phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase/protein kinase B signal transduction
GO:0051897.definition: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase/protein kinase B signal transduction.

GO:0043001.name: Golgi to plasma membrane protein transport
GO:0043001.definition: The directed movement of proteins from the Golgi to the plasma membrane in transport vesicles that move from the trans-Golgi network to the plasma membrane. Golgi to plasma membrane transport precedes exocytosis.

GO:0032483.name: regulation of Rab protein signal transduction
GO:0032483.definition: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of Rab protein signal transduction.

GO:1902017.name: regulation of cilium assembly
GO:1902017.definition: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of cilium assembly.

GO:0042802.name: identical protein binding
GO:0042802.definition: Binding to an identical protein or proteins.

GO:0019894.name: kinesin binding
GO:0019894.definition: Interacting selectively and non-covalently and stoichiometrically with kinesin, a member of a superfamily of microtubule-based motor proteins that perform force-generating tasks such as organelle transport and chromosome segregation.

GO:0031267.name: small GTPase binding
GO:0031267.definition: Binding to a small monomeric GTPase.

GO:0032014.name: positive regulation of ARF protein signal transduction
GO:0032014.definition: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of ARF protein signal transduction.

GO:0032588.name: trans-Golgi network membrane
GO:0032588.definition: The lipid bilayer surrounding any of the compartments that make up the trans-Golgi network.

GO:0030674.name: protein-macromolecule adaptor activity
GO:0030674.definition: An adaptor activity that brings together two or more macromolecules in contact, permitting those molecules to function in a coordinated way. The adaptor can bring together two proteins, or a protein and another macromolecule such as a lipid or a nucleic acid.
GO:0030674.comment: Note that protein complex scaffolds should use GO:0140378 protein complex scaffold activity.

GO:0006893.name: Golgi to plasma membrane transport
GO:0006893.definition: The directed movement of substances from the Golgi to the plasma membrane in transport vesicles that move from the trans-Golgi network to the plasma membrane. Golgi to plasma membrane transport precedes exocytosis.

GO:0032266.name: phosphatidylinositol-3-phosphate binding
GO:0032266.definition: Binding to phosphatidylinositol-3-phosphate, a derivative of phosphatidylinositol in which the inositol ring is phosphorylated at the 3' position.

GO:0051018.name: protein kinase A binding
GO:0051018.definition: Binding to a protein kinase A.
GO:0051018.comment: Note that this term is a direct child of 'protein binding ; GO:0005515' because it encompasses binding to either the catalytic or regulatory subunit of protein kinase A, and the latter does not have kinase activity.
